mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares observations made in an inertial reference frame with those in a non‑inertial reference frame?

options.A: In an inertial frame, a body at rest remains at rest; in a non‑inertial frame, a body at rest may appear to accelerate without any real force.
options.B: In an inertial frame, fictitious forces must be introduced; in a non‑inertial frame, Newton’s laws hold without modification.
options.C: Both frames require the same set of forces to explain motion.
options.D: In a non‑inertial frame, the law of conservation of momentum does not hold, whereas it always holds in an inertial frame.

mcqs.answer: In an inertial frame, a body at rest remains at rest; in a non‑inertial frame, a body at rest may appear to accelerate without any real force.
mcqs.explanation: An inertial reference frame obeys Newton’s first law: a body at rest or moving uniformly stays so unless acted upon by a real force. In a non‑inertial (accelerating) frame, observers must introduce fictitious forces to explain why a body that is actually at rest in an inertial frame appears to accelerate. Options B, C and D misstate the role of fictitious forces and conservation laws.

mcqs.question: In a straight line, particle P is at x = 5 m and particle Q is at x = 12 m measured from the same origin. What is the relative position of Q with respect to P?
mcqs.explanation: Relative position of Q with respect to P is given by r_QP = x_Q – x_P = 12 m – 5 m = +7 m. The positive sign indicates that Q lies 7 m ahead of P in the chosen positive direction. The other options either give the wrong magnitude or opposite sign.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines relative velocity?

options.A: The velocity of a body measured in a reference frame that is itself moving relative to an observer.
options.B: The sum of the velocities of two bodies irrespective of the observer.
options.C: The velocity of a body relative only to the Earth’s surface.
options.D: The average of the velocities of two bodies moving in opposite directions.

mcqs.answer: The velocity of a body measured in a reference frame that is itself moving relative to an observer.
mcqs.explanation: Relative velocity is the velocity of an object as observed from a reference frame that may itself be in motion. It is obtained by vector subtraction of the observer’s (or reference frame’s) velocity from the object’s velocity. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Train A moves east at 60 km/h and Train B moves east at 40 km/h on parallel tracks. What is the speed of Train A relative to Train B?
mcqs.explanation: Relative speed = speed of A – speed of B (since both move in the same direction) = 60 km/h – 40 km/h = 20 km/h. The other options either add the speeds or ignore the direction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an inertial reference frame from a non‑inertial reference frame?

options.A: In an inertial frame, Newton’s first law holds without fictitious forces; in a non‑inertial frame, fictitious forces must be introduced to apply Newton’s laws.
options.B: In an inertial frame, objects require external forces to remain at rest; in a non‑inertial frame, objects remain at rest without forces.
options.C: Both frames describe motion in exactly the same way, requiring no additional concepts.
options.D: In a non‑inertial frame, time dilation occurs, while in an inertial frame it does not.

mcqs.answer: In an inertial frame, Newton’s first law holds without fictitious forces; in a non‑inertial frame, fictitious forces must be introduced to apply Newton’s laws.
mcqs.explanation: An inertial frame is one where bodies obey Newton’s laws directly; no fictitious forces are needed. In accelerating (non‑inertial) frames, observers must add fictitious forces (e.g., centrifugal, Coriolis) to use Newton’s laws. Options B, C, and D are incorrect descriptions of reference frames.

mcqs.question: A cyclist is 30 m ahead of a pedestrian on the same straight road. What is the relative position of the cyclist with respect to the pedestrian?
mcqs.explanation: Relative position = position of cyclist – position of pedestrian = +30 m, indicating the cyclist is 30 m in the positive direction ahead of the pedestrian. Negative values would imply the opposite direction, which is not the case here.

mcqs.question: A boat moves north at 5 m/s relative to still water. The river flows east at 3 m/s. What is the magnitude of the boat’s velocity relative to the riverbank?
mcqs.explanation: The velocity vectors are perpendicular: north component = 5 m/s, east component = 3 m/s. Magnitude = √(5² + 3²) = √(25 + 9) = √34 m/s ≈ 5.83 m/s. Option A adds the components linearly, which is incorrect for perpendicular vectors. Options C and D are unrelated magnitudes.

mcqs.question: Two cyclists start 200 m apart on a straight road and move towards each other. Cyclist 1 travels at 5 m/s and Cyclist 2 at 7 m/s. How long will it take for them to meet?
mcqs.explanation: When moving towards each other, their relative speed = 5 m/s + 7 m/s = 12 m/s. Time to meet = distance / relative speed = 200 m / 12 m/s ≈ 16.67 s, which rounds to 16.7 s. The other options correspond to incorrect relative speeds or arithmetic errors.
